verses.45:15: {vere}, vós sois um Deus escondido, * Deus de Israel, Salvador.
verses.45:16: Foram envergonhados, e coraram todos: * juntos {abierunt} os {fabricatores} de erros.
verses.45:17: Israel foi salvo no Senhor com salvação eterna: * não sereis envergonhados, e não corareis {saeculi}.
verses.45:18: Porque isto diz o Senhor, {creans}, * o próprio Deus que {formans} a terra e a {faciens}, {plastes}:
verses.45:19: Não a criou em vão, formou-a para que fosse habitada: * Eu sou o Senhor, e não há outro.
verses.45:20: Não falei {abscondito}, * num lugar tenebroso da terra:
verses.45:21: {frustra}: * eu sou o Senhor, que falo justiça, que anuncio {recta}.
verses.45:22: Reuni-vos, e vinde, e aproximai-vos juntos, * vós que fostes salvos dentre as nações:
verses.45:23: {nescierunt} os que levantam {lignum}, * e rogam a um deus que não salva.
verses.45:24: Anunciai, e vinde, e {consiliamini} juntos: * Quem {auditum} desde o início, desde então o predisse?
verses.45:25: Acaso não sou eu o Senhor, e não há mais Deus além de mim? * Deus justo e que salve não há {praeter}.
verses.45:26: {convertimini} a mim, e sereis salvos, todos os confins da terra: * porque eu sou Deus, e não há outro.
verses.45:27: Por mim mesmo jurei: sairá da minha boca a palavra de justiça, * e não {revertetur}:
verses.45:28: Porque a mim {curvabitur} todo joelho, * e {jurabit} toda língua.
verses.45:29: Portanto, dirá: No Senhor estão {justitiae} e o domínio: * a ele virão, e serão envergonhados todos os que lhe resistem.
verses.45:30: No Senhor será justificada e {laudabitur} * toda a descendência de Israel.

decisions.why: The adverb opens the canticle and is said aloud at the head of Friday Lauds. MS1932 'verdadeiramente'; DM1962 'Em verdade'; the CNBB Liturgia das Horas 'realmente' (circulation.md). 'Tu es' is the subject named, as the Latin names it: 'vós sois'.

options.label: Em verdade
options.note: Draft. Plain and biblical ('Em verdade vos digo'); three syllables for the Latin's two, where 'Verdadeiramente' is six and puts the colon +4 on the Latin. DM1962 has it, at the head of this same Latin.

options.label: Verdadeiramente
options.note: MS1932's word and the closest adverb; long at the head of a line meant for one breath.

options.label: Na verdade
options.note: Refused: in current Brazilian speech 'na verdade' means 'actually, in fact' and corrects what went before.

decisions.why: abíre is 'go away, depart'; in + accusative is motion into. confúsio → 'vergonha' as confúndi → 'ser envergonhado' in the first colon (D15; 39:16, 68:20, 70:13, 131:18 have confúsio → vergonha). simul → 'juntos' (the working row).

options.label: partiram para a vergonha
options.note: v2 (stylist): keeps the going-away of ab-íre without the chime of passive "Foram" against "se foram" in one verse.

options.label: se foram para a vergonha
options.note: Draft. 'ir-se' keeps the going-away of ab-íre; 'para' the motion of in + accusative.

options.label: foram para a vergonha
options.note: Shorter; loses the 'away' of ab-.

options.label: caíram na vergonha
options.note: Idiomatic, but 'fall' is another image than the Latin's going (rule 2).

decisions.why: The makers of 'errors' — the idols, but the Latin says errors, and the image stays (MS1932 glosses '(ou ídolos)'; DM1962 'fabricadores de ídolos' follows the Hebrew-family sense). The verb fabricári has 'formar' (73:16) and 'forjar' (128:3) in the glossary; formar is formáre's here (45:18), so it cannot serve.

options.label: fabricantes
options.note: Draft; MS1932 'os fabricantes de erros', DRB 'forgers of errors'. The cognate; a stylist once heard factories in 'fabricastes' (73:16) — here, of idol-makers, the workshop is the point.

options.label: forjadores
options.note: The 128:3 verb (forjaram) as a noun: craft and contriving at once, as DRB's 'forgers'. Rarer as a noun.

options.label: artífices
options.note: Dignified; proparoxytone, and it would praise them.

decisions.why: Two glossary rows meet: in sǽculum sǽculi → 'pelos séculos dos séculos' (D27) and usque in ætérnum / in sǽculum → 'para todo o sempre' (D37: usque is carried by 'todo'). The phrase usque in sǽculum sǽculi has no precedent in the finished psalms (concord.py). The Hebrew-family CNBB LH has 'eternamente pelos séculos'.

options.label: pelos séculos dos séculos
options.note: Draft: D27's formula, the words the Latin has; usque ('all the way') is left inside 'pelos', which already says 'throughout'. MS1932 'pelos séculos dos séculos'. The colon ends on a proparoxytone, as the Latin's does (sǽculi).

options.label: para todo o sempre
options.note: D37 extended; keeps usque but drops the doubled sǽculum.

options.label: até os séculos dos séculos
options.note: usque as 'até'; the formula bent out of shape.

decisions.latin: Dóminus creans cælos … Deus formans terram, et fáciens eam
decisions.why: Three present participles (creans, formans, fáciens) used as titles: the one who creates, forms, makes. The next verse turns them into perfects of the same acts (creávit eam … formávit eam), so the creating is a done thing. Portuguese has no present participle for this; a relative clause must choose a tense. DRB 'that created … that formed'; MS1932 'que criou … que formou'; DM1962 'criador dos céus'.

options.label: que cria
options.note: v2 (latinist): the Latin's present, for all three participles (cria, forma, faz): a title of the Creator, timeless as the participle is; the perfects follow in 45:19 as in the Latin.

options.label: que criou
options.note: Draft: the past, as DRB and MS1932, and as 45:19 itself says it (creávit, formávit); 'que formou … e a fez' follow in the second colon.

options.label: criador dos céus
options.note: DM1962's noun: timeless like the participle, but a noun for a verb, and the other two participles would have to follow.

decisions.why: plastes (πλάστης) is 'a moulder, potter, modeller' — L&S cites this verse under the ecclesiastical sense 'creator, maker'. The Latin makes it a noun in apposition, and repeats ipse (ipse Deus … ipse plastes). The Hebrew has 'he established it' (MS1932 'que a dispôs assim', DM1962 'consolidou' — Hebrew family). The glossary gives plasmáre → 'moldar' (118:73, the potter's verb, same Greek root). 'o próprio … ele próprio' keeps the repeated ipse.

options.label: ele próprio, o seu modelador
options.note: v2 (latinist): the Latin's noun in apposition kept (DRB "the very maker thereof"); the moulding kept in the word; oxytone before the colon. The comma after "ele próprio" marks the apposition.

options.label: ele próprio a moldou
options.note: v1: the noun made a verb; the latinist: a fourth finite act in the list, where the Latin has a noun.

options.label: ele próprio o seu artífice
options.note: A noun, L&S's 'maker'; loses the moulding, and ends on a proparoxytone.

decisions.why: in abscóndito is a place in 26:5 and 30:21 (no lugar escondido, the row) and a manner in 9:30a (às escondidas). With a verb of speaking the manner is the usual sense (DRB "in secret", MS1932 "às ocultas"); the v2 Latinist reads it as a place, parallel to in loco terræ tenebróso.

options.label: às escondidas
options.note: Draft: the manner, as 9:30a; the second colon names the place, so the parallel is still heard; keeps the root of "escondido" (45:15) — the hidden God did not speak in hiding.

options.label: em lugar escondido
options.note: The v2 Latinist's fix: the place, as the 26:5 row; doubles "lugar" with the next colon.

decisions.latin: Non dixi sémini Jacob frustra: Quǽrite me
decisions.why: Where does frustra belong? In the Latin it stands between 'I did not say to the seed of Jacob' and 'Seek me', so it can go with either: 'I did not say in vain … Seek me' or 'I did not say … Seek me in vain' (DRB moves it into the quotation; the Hebrew has tohu 'in emptiness' before 'seek me', DM1962 'em vão me procurareis'). The Latin's order leaves it open; so does the draft's. semen → 'descendência' (D32; no plant image here).

options.label: Não disse à descendência de Jacó em vão: Buscai-me

forms.frustra: Não disse à descendência de Jacó em vão: Buscai-me

options.note: Draft: the Latin's order, the adverb between the two, open both ways. quǽrere → 'buscar' (glossary); 'Buscai' ≠ 'busquei' (rule 3).

options.label: Não disse em vão à descendência de Jacó: Buscai-me

forms.frustra: Não disse em vão à descendência de Jacó: Buscai-me

options.note: Resolves it: the saying was not in vain.

options.label: Não disse à descendência de Jacó: Buscai-me em vão

forms.frustra: Não disse à descendência de Jacó: Buscai-me em vão

options.note: DRB's reading; resolves it the other way, and puts a Hebrew sense on the Latin.

decisions.why: A neuter plural adjective as object: 'right things'. loquens justítiam → 'que falo justiça', the accusative of content without article as 57:2 (justítiam loquímini → falais justiça). ego Dóminus → 'eu sou o Senhor' (the copula supplied, as in 45:19 and 45:26).

options.label: o que é reto
options.note: Draft; MS1932 'o que é recto'. The glossary notes 'o que é reto' was once heard as 'assess' beside judging (57:2); beside 'anunciar' there is no such risk.

options.label: coisas retas
options.note: Word for word (DRB 'right things'); a noun supplied, as 2:1 'coisas vãs'.

options.label: a retidão
options.note: A noun for the adjective; retidão is diréctio's word (glossary).

decisions.why: Absolute: 'they have not known' — they are without knowledge (DRB 'they have no knowledge'; MS1932 'insensatos se têm mostrado'). 81:5 has the same word at the head of a verse: 'Não souberam, nem entenderam'.

options.label: Nada souberam
options.note: v2 (stylist): the Latin's perfect, absolute; "Nada" makes the negation absolute as Portuguese says it ("Não souberam" alone asks "what?", where 81:5 has "nem entenderam" to complete it).

options.label: Não souberam
options.note: v1, as 81:5; heard as unfinished when it stands alone (stylist).

options.label: Nada sabem
options.note: The stative sense, and 'nada' gives the absolute verb an object Portuguese likes; supplies a word.

options.label: Não têm conhecimento
options.note: DRB's build; heard as office language ('não tenho conhecimento').

decisions.why: 'The wood of their carving'. lignum here is not a tree (the glossary's 'árvore' is for the living tree, 1:3) but the carved block. sculptúra → the glossary has sculptília → 'imagens esculpidas' and notes that 'esculturas' was heard as art. leváre → 'levantar' (glossary): both lifting up and setting up, as levant can be (DRB 'set up'; the LXX and Hebrew 'carry').

options.label: o seu lenho esculpido
options.note: Draft: wood and carving both kept, the genitive made an adjective (grammar); 'lenho' is a piece of wood, known from the Santo Lenho; the colon is +2 on the Latin.

options.label: a sua madeira esculpida
options.note: Plainer word; 'madeira' is the material rather than the block.

options.label: o lenho da sua escultura
options.note: The Latin's genitive kept; +4 on the Latin, and 'escultura' leans to art.

decisions.why: consiliári, 'to take counsel, consult' (L&S). The glossary's open row gives 'planejar' from 30:14, its only psalm place, where the wicked plot to take a life; here the nations are summoned to deliberate together, with no object — 'planejai juntos' would ask what they are to plan. DRB 'consult together'; MS1932 'tomai conselho'. Departing from the row here; the row stays for plotting.

options.label: tomai conselho
options.note: Draft: keeps consílium's word ('conselho', D33) inside the verb's rendering; MS1932 has it.

options.label: planejai
options.note: The glossary row (30:14); wants an object here.

options.label: aconselhai-vos
options.note: One verb for one; 'aconselhar-se' is 'seek advice from someone', which the summons does not mean.

decisions.why: audítum fácere, 'to make heard' (the Hebrew causative 'who announced'); audítus elsewhere is the hearing (D44, 50:10). DRB 'who hath declared this'. The Latin then goes on without a conjunction (ex tunc prædíxit illud); v2 keeps the asyndeton (latinist: v1's 'e' joined what the Latin leaves as two parallel phrases). ab inítio → 'desde o início' (glossary; 73:2, 76:12); ex tunc → 'desde então' (75:8, 92:2).

options.label: fez ouvir isto
options.note: Draft: the Latin's build (fácere + the hearing), plain Portuguese.

options.label: deu a ouvir isto
options.note: Also idiomatic; 'dar' is not the Latin's verb.

options.label: anunciou isto
options.note: DRB's and MS1932's sense; 'anunciar' is annuntiáre's, which stands at the head of this very verse — two Latin words would merge.

decisions.why: Two prepositions in one verse: absque me → 'além de mim' (ultra → 'mais', as 9:39, 82:5); præter me → 'senão eu', as præter in 17:32 (quis Deus præter Dóminum → quem é Deus senão o Senhor). salvans (participle) is kept apart from Salvátor (45:15): 'que salve'.

options.label: senão eu
options.note: Draft: 17:32's 'senão'; keeps the two prepositions two.

options.label: fora de mim
options.note: MS1932 ('não o há fora de mim'); keeps 'mim' as the Latin keeps me; 'estar fora de mim' is also 'to be beside myself'.

options.label: além de mim
options.note: The same words as absque me in the first colon: two Latin prepositions merged.

decisions.why: convértere → 'voltar' is the glossary's verb, with D25's exception: 'converter' where men are told to turn to God (7:13 'Se não vos converterdes'). This is that case: the ends of the earth summoned to God. The Brazilian LH and Lectionary have 'Voltai-vos para mim' (circulation.md).

options.label: Convertei-vos
options.note: Draft: D25's exception, the Latin's own word; 'convertei' ≠ 'converti' (rule 3).

options.label: Voltai-vos
options.note: The row's verb and the Brazilian liturgical wording; 'Voltai-vos' is also what the psalter says to God (6:5), so the address could blur.

decisions.why: 'And it shall not return' — the word that goes out of the mouth does not come back (cf. Isa 55:11, not quoted here). The Brazilian Lectionary has 'a palavra que não volta atrás' (circulation.md), the idiom for not revoking; MS1932 'não será revogada' explains.

options.label: voltará
options.note: Draft: the Latin's image, and the verb revérti has in 103:29 and 145:4.

options.label: voltará atrás
options.note: The Lectionary's idiom: clearer, but 'atrás' supplies the sense of revoking the Latin leaves as an image.

options.label: será revogada
options.note: MS1932: an explanation, not the Latin's word.

decisions.why: Quoted by Paul (Rom 14:11, Phil 2:10), but in other Latin words: flectétur (Rom), flectátur (Phil) — see circulation.md. Isaiah's Latin has curváre, which the glossary renders 'curvar' (incurváre 56:7; curvátus 37:7). For a knee Portuguese says 'dobrar'; every Brazilian text seen has it (LH, Lectionary, DM1962, MS1932). mihi is a dative: 'a mim'. omne genu → 'todo joelho' without article ('todo o joelho' in Brazil is 'the whole knee').

options.label: se dobrará
options.note: Draft: what a knee does in Portuguese, and what the Brazilian ear knows of this line; the glossary's 'curvar' is kept for the bending of backs and souls.

options.label: se curvará
options.note: The glossary's verb for the root; 'curvar o joelho' is understood but not said.

decisions.why: Isaiah's Latin says 'shall swear' (the Hebrew likewise). Paul quotes the line from the Greek, where the tongue 'confesses' (LXX ἐξομολογήσεται; Vulgate Rom 14:11 confitébitur, Phil 2:11 confiteátur). The Latin being translated is Isaiah's, so the tongue swears — as in the Brazilian LH and Lectionary, which also keep 'jurar'.

options.label: jurará
options.note: Draft: the Latin's verb, echoing 'jurei' at the head of 45:27.

options.label: confessará
options.note: Paul's verb (Rom 14:11, Phil 2:11), refused: it is not in this Latin, and it would break the echo with 45:27 'jurávi'.

decisions.why: The plural justítiæ with meæ, and impérium without a possessive. The finished psalms keep the plural 'as minhas justiças' (49:16, 88:32; 147:8 'as suas justiças'). impérium → 'domínio' (the open row, 85:16; canticle 211, 29:12b). 'dicet' is left without a subject, as the Latin leaves it. ergo → 'Portanto' (72:13 has 'Então', where it is a thought; here it draws a consequence).

options.label: as minhas justiças
options.note: Draft: the Latin's number, as 49:16 and 88:32.

options.label: a minha justiça
options.note: The singular: plainer, 'justiças' can be heard as courts; the number is lost.

decisions.why: 33:3 has the same build: In Dómino laudábitur ánima mea → 'No Senhor será louvada a minha alma'. laudáre → 'louvar' (the laus row). The Brazilian Lectionary and DM1962 antiphon say 'será justificada e glorificada toda a descendência de Israel'; 'glorificar' is glorificáre's word (85:9). justificábitur → 'será justificada' as 142:2 'non justificábitur … omnis vivens → será justificado'; the active 'justificar' was heard as 'make excuses' (glossary, 72:13, 81:3), the passive of God's justifying is not.

options.label: louvada
options.note: Draft: the Latin's word, as 33:3.

options.label: glorificada
options.note: The Brazilian Lectionary and DM1962 wording; another Latin word's.

choices.45:15: DO's file opens with the heading line '(Canticum Isaiæ * Isa 45:15-30)'; it is not a verse (readVerses skips it) and is not translated (D7, as ps233, ps211). If a Portuguese file is made for DO, the heading would read '(Cântico de Isaías * Isa 45:15-30)' — DO's range is its own line numbering; the text is Isa 45:15–25 of the Vulgate. 'Deus abscónditus' → 'um Deus escondido': the article supplied (DRB 'a hidden God'; MS1932, DM1962 'um Deus escondido'), the plain adjective as every Brazilian text has it. 'Salvátor' → 'Salvador' (the salvátor row, 24:5), capitalised as a title.
choices.45:16: confúndi → 'ser envergonhado' (D15), erubéscere → 'corar' (the working row; 6:11, 82:18): 'Foram envergonhados, e coraram'. The Latin's order, subject last ('todos'), is also good Portuguese. The subject is not named in the Latin; not supplied (DM1962 'os seus adversários' follows the LXX). The stylist asked for 'Todos foram envergonhados': not taken — 'coraram todos' is good Portuguese and keeps omnes where the Latin puts it.
choices.45:17: salvátus … salúte: the figura (salvo … salvação) kept; no article before 'salvação eterna', as the Latin (v2, stylist: v1's 'uma' limped). non confundémini, et non erubescétis → the same pair of verbs as 45:16. Addressed to Israel, plural (vós).
choices.45:18: hæc dicit Dóminus → 'isto diz o Senhor' (the Brazilian Lectionary opens the same verse 'Isto diz o Senhor'; 11:6a 'diz o Senhor'). ipse Deus → 'o próprio Deus', and the second ipse 'ele próprio' (decision plastes), so the repetition stands. cælos plural → 'os céus'. formáre → 'formar', fácere → 'fazer' (94:5, 138:5), in the present with creans (decision creans). Both cola end on an oxytone (céus, modelador), which the brief allows. v2: colon 2 is +3 on the Latin, the cost of keeping plastes a noun with its possessive (decision plastes); accepted.
choices.45:19: The Latin sets two clauses back to back without a conjunction (non in vanum creávit eam, ut habitarétur, formávit eam); the natural order puts the purpose after 'formou-a' (D2, order). in vanum → 'em vão' (the working row). Ego Dóminus, et non est álius → 'Eu sou o Senhor, e não há outro', identical at 45:26b ('eu sou Deus, e não há outro'), and kept apart from ultra (45:25, 'mais') and præter.
choices.45:20: in abscóndito → 'às escondidas', as 9:30a (the same Latin phrase, adverbial); it keeps the root of 'escondido' (45:15): the hidden God did not speak in hiding. The glossary's 'no lugar escondido' (26:5, 30:21) is for a hidden place; here the second colon names the place. tenebrósus → 'tenebroso' as 17:12 ('água tenebrosa') and 87:7; a blind reader once listed 'tenebrosos' as unknown — 'escuro' is the plainer word if a reader stumbles.
choices.45:22: congregári → 'reunir-se' (D43); 'Reuni-vos' carries the enclitic, so D13 allows it though 'reuni' is also 'I gathered'. accédite → 'aproximai-vos' (33:6), simul → 'juntos'. The polysyndeton (et … et) kept. qui salváti estis → 'vós que fostes salvos': the subject named. ex géntibus → 'dentre as nações' (gentes → nações).
choices.45:23: rogáre → 'rogar' (121:6). deum lowercase, as the Latin prints it: a god that does not save. 'não salva' against 'Salvador' / 'salvos': the Latin's word-family runs through the canticle (salvátor, salvátus, salus, salváti, salvántem, salvans, salvi) and is kept in one Portuguese family. Colon 1 is +4 syllables on the Latin (v2, with 'Nada'): 'os que levantam' for qui levant, and the genitive sculptúræ made an adjective (decision lignum). Accepted.
choices.45:24: annuntiáre → 'anunciar' (D41); 'Anunciai' ≠ 'anunciei'. Colon 1 is −3 syllables on the Latin, colon 2 +2. Colon 1's −3 is the Latin's long consiliámini against 'tomai conselho'. The stylist asked for 'aconselhai-vos': not taken (decision consiliamini; the ambiguity reader heard 'tomai conselho juntos' as 'deliberate', the sense wanted). The two 'desde' are the Latin's two parallel phrases (ab inítio, ex tunc).
choices.45:25: numquid → 'acaso' (the open row, 7:12; the Lectionary has 'Acaso não sou eu o Senhor?'). 'Deus justo e que salve não há senão eu' (v2: the commas dropped, stylist; one breath, one claim): the subjunctive in a negated relative; the participle salvans kept apart from Salvátor.
choices.45:26: omnes fines terræ → 'todos os confins da terra' (21:28, 66:7b, 94:4). quia → 'porque'.
choices.45:27: juráre in → 'jurar por' (62:12); in memetípso → 'por mim mesmo'. The comma after jurávi is made a colon: what follows is the oath's content (punctuation is grammar). justítiæ verbum → 'a palavra de justiça' (verbum → palavra); the article supplied. Colon 1 is −3 on the Latin (memetípso, egrediétur are long words). Colon 2 ends on an oxytone, 'voltará'.
choices.45:28: Quia → 'Porque'. Both cola keep the Latin's order, verb before subject, so the two lines answer each other as in the Latin.
choices.45:29: dicet → 'dirá', moved before what is said (v2, stylist: the parenthetical was unsayable; order yields to the ear, D2; DRB does the same), no subject supplied (DM1962 'dirão', MS1932 'Dir-se-á' both decide). ad eum vénient → 'a ele virão' (85:9 'virão'). repugnáre → 'resistir' (DRB 'resist', the Brazilian Lectionary 'os que lhe resistem'); the one place in the corpus, no glossary row. confundéntur → 'serão envergonhados' (D15).
choices.45:30: omne semen Israël → 'toda a descendência de Israel' (D32: offspring, no plant image; 'toda a' = the whole, which a collective wants). The Brazilian Lectionary line is 'no Senhor será justificada e glorificada toda a descendência de Israel': the draft differs only in 'louvada' (decision laudabitur). Colon 2 is +4 on the Latin: 'descendência' for the one-syllable semen (D32) and the article of 'toda a'. Accepted; no shorter word keeps D32. Colon 1 does not repeat 'será' before 'louvada': the Latin repeats the verb form in two words (justificábitur, laudábitur), Portuguese carries both on one auxiliary. v2: no comma before 'e louvada' (stylist).
choices.45:21: Colon 2 is +4 syllables on the Latin (checks.py): the copula 'sou' and two relative 'que' are supplied for two participles (loquens, annúntians) Portuguese cannot keep as participles; 'o que é reto' adds one more (decision recta). Accepted. The stylist asked to move 'em vão' beside the verb: not taken, it is the decision frustra (the ambiguity reader heard both readings open). 'que falo justiça' stays with 57:2.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm215.txt (DO files the canticles as Psalms 210–273; Friday Lauds I in the Roman psalter). Its sixteen line ids 45:15–45:30 are DO's own: the text is Isa 45:15–25 of the Vulgate (DO splits Vulgate 45:18, 20, 21, 23 each in two). Compared with the Clementine Vulgate from Bolls (consult/ps215/bolls-VULG-23-45.json): the same words. The heading line '(Canticum Isaiæ * Isa 45:15-30)' is not a verse and is left out (D7). render.py and checks.py take the DO number 215 unchanged (they read the file by number and key on its ids). parallels.py handles psalm numbers only, so ps215/show_parallels.py builds consult/parallels/ps215.md (gitignored) (Vulgate, DRB, WLC from Bolls; LXX from consult/lxx-*.csv; MS1932 from the pdftotext text layer of printed pp. 494–495, consult/ps215/ms1932-isa45-p494-495.txt; DM1962 Friday Lauds festive canticle; DO Portuguese, no authority), as ps211 and ps214 did. concord.py and gloss.py are local helpers (concord copied from ps211). The Latin here is Jerome's Isaiah from the Hebrew, not the Gallican psalter: the LXX is a distant witness (its 45:15 'and we did not know', 45:20–21 differ widely) and was not followed where it differs.

Canticle-level draft from the parallels, the glossary and concord.py precedents (81:5 Nesciérunt; 33:3 In Dómino laudábitur; 142:2 justificábitur; 17:32 præter; 9:30a in abscóndito; 49:16, 88:32 justítias meas; 85:16 impérium; 7:13 D25 convertímini). Brazilian circulation fetched and recorded in circulation.md (CNBB LH Friday Lauds I; Lectionary, Advent III Wednesday, Is 45,6b-8.18.21b-25). Hard readings: plastes (45:18), the position of frustra (45:21), audítum fecit (45:24), the Pauline line (45:28: Isaiah's Latin says jurábit, Paul's confitébitur), meæ justítiæ (45:29).

render.py and checks.py run with DO number 215 unchanged (no shared tool failed on the canticle). Hard checks pass: ids and pointing match the Latin. Soft flags: length +4 at 45:21b and 45:30b, +3 at 45:23a, −3 at 45:24a and 45:27a; each explained in choices and accepted. Output in checks.md.

Draft 1, read by claude-opus-5-5 in a fresh context with latin.json (run by the coordinator). No majors; three minors, all taken. It called the translation faithful in sense, tense, voice, person and number, and passed the open placement of frustra (45:21).

outcomes.remark: creans, formans, fáciens are present participles; v1 put them in the past (que criou, formou, fez)
outcomes.reason: The present is as timeless as the participle; the perfects of the same acts follow in 45:19, as in the Latin.

outcomes.remark: plastes is a noun; v1 made it a fourth finite verb (ele próprio a moldou); asks ele próprio, o seu modelador
outcomes.reason: The apposition is the Latin's build, and with the present tense the verb would have to be "a molda", a fourth act in the list. v1's verb stays option 2.

outcomes.remark: "e desde então" adds a conjunction the Latin lacks
outcomes.reason: The two phrases (ab inítio, ex tunc) stand side by side in the Latin; the asyndeton is sayable.

audit.note: Draft 1, claude-opus-5-5, fresh context, with latin.json. Eight verses remarked; five changes taken, the rest refused where a decision or precedent holds them. Best line 45:28, worst 45:29 (taken).

outcomes.remark: "Foram envergonhados … se foram" chimes two verbs; asks partiram, and "Todos foram envergonhados e coraram"
outcomes.reason: "partiram" keeps the going-away of ab-íre without the chime. The reordering of "todos" is refused: "coraram todos" is good Portuguese and keeps omnes where the Latin puts it.

outcomes.remark: "com uma salvação eterna": the article limps
outcomes.reason: The Latin has none (salúte ætérna); one syllable fewer in a long colon.

outcomes.remark: "em vão" stranded after Jacó; asks "Não disse em vão à descendência de Jacó"
outcomes.reason: The placement is the decision: the Latin sets frustra between the saying and the quotation, and the ambiguity reader heard both readings. His order is option 2.

outcomes.remark: "que falo justiça" stiff; asks "que digo a justiça"
outcomes.reason: loquens justítiam as 57:2 (justítiam loquímini → falais justiça); "dizer a justiça" adds an article and is heard as "telling (someone) justice".

outcomes.remark: bare "Não souberam" sounds unfinished; asks "Nada souberam"
outcomes.reason: Keeps the perfect; "Nada" gives the absolute verb the absolute Portuguese form. 81:5's "Não souberam" is completed there by "nem entenderam", which is absent here.

outcomes.remark: "tomai conselho" bookish; asks "aconselhai-vos"
outcomes.reason: "aconselhar-se" is heard as "seek advice from someone"; the ambiguity reader heard "tomai conselho juntos" as "deliberate", the sense wanted. His form is option 3.

outcomes.remark: two "desde" blur; asks "desde o princípio, e já desde então"
outcomes.reason: The two phrases are the Latin's parallel (ab inítio, ex tunc; "desde o início" as 73:2, 76:12; "desde então" as 75:8, 92:2); the latinist asked for no conjunction here.

outcomes.remark: commas chop the colon; asks "Deus justo e que salve não há fora de mim"
outcomes.reason: The commas are dropped. "fora de mim" is refused (option 2): it would lose "senão" for præter (17:32) and can be heard as "beside myself".

outcomes.remark: parenthetical "dirá" unsayable; asks "Portanto, dirá: No Senhor estão …"
outcomes.reason: Order yields to the ear (D2); every word kept, the speaker still unnamed; DRB does the same.

outcomes.remark: comma before "e louvada" stops the voice twice before the mediant
outcomes.reason: Punctuation only.

audit.note: Draft 1, Portuguese only, claude-opus-5-5, fresh context. Twenty-four items, four unknown words. Only 45:25 led to a change (with the stylist).

outcomes.remark: frustra heard both as "did not speak in vain" and "seek me in vain"
outcomes.reason: The Latin's own openness, kept on purpose.

outcomes.remark: "fabricantes de erros": the idol sense is not audible
outcomes.reason: The Latin says errors, not idols (rule 2); 45:23 names the carved wood.

outcomes.remark: with commas, heard as two claims
outcomes.reason: Commas dropped (with the stylist).

outcomes.remark: speaker of "dirá" unclear; "as minhas justiças" heard as God's
outcomes.reason: The Latin leaves dicet without a subject; v2 moves the verb first, which does not name him.

outcomes.remark: "domínio" as a territory
outcomes.reason: Heard first as power/rule; impérium → domínio (85:16; canticle 211, 29:12b).

outcomes.remark: unknown words coraram, lenho, rogam, confins
outcomes.reason: Glossary rows or settled precedent: corar (erubéscere), rogar (121:6), confins (21:28, 66:7b); lenho is decision lignum ("madeira" option 2).

outcomes.remark: addressee of "sereis", who "fostes salvos", vocative vs subject, "não voltará", justified/praised
outcomes.reason: Each is the Latin's own openness; the heard reading is the intended one or one the Latin also allows.

audit.note: v2: 45:16 partiram; 45:17 no article; 45:18 present tense (cria, forma, faz) and the noun "o seu modelador"; 45:23 "Nada souberam"; 45:24 asyndeton; 45:25 commas dropped; 45:29 "dirá" moved before the saying; 45:30 comma dropped. Downloaded third-party texts moved to consult/ps215/ and the parallels to consult/parallels/ps215.md (gitignored; the repo is public); show_parallels.py, circulation.md and these notes repointed.
Draft 2: hard pass. Soft flags: length +4 at 45:21b, 45:23a (Nada added) and 45:30b; +3 at 45:18b (the noun o seu modelador); −3 at 45:24a and 45:27a. Each explained in choices and accepted.

Draft 2, claude-opus-5-5 in a fresh context with latin.json (run by the coordinator). No majors; two minors on two verses, all held as options. It called the rendering close and faithful, tenses, voices and persons tracking the Latin, and passed fabricatóres errórum, plastes, justítiæ plural and the open dicet. Gate clean of majors.

outcomes.remark: in abscóndito is local, parallel to in loco terræ tenebróso; asks "Não falei em lugar escondido"
outcomes.reason: With a verb of speaking, the adverbial sense is DRB's and MS1932's; 9:30a has the same phrase adverbially; the place is named in the next colon, and "em lugar escondido, num lugar tenebroso" doubles "lugar". His form is option 2.

outcomes.remark: "Nada souberam" adds an intensifying "nothing"; asks "Não souberam"
outcomes.reason: Held for Gustavo: the v1 stylist asked for "Nada" because bare "Não souberam" sounds unfinished in Portuguese; the v2 Latinist asks it back. The Latin's absolute verb has no object in either; "Não souberam" (81:5) is option 2.

outcomes.remark: lignum sculptúræ suæ: the genitive made an adjective; asks "o lenho da sua escultura"
outcomes.reason: He calls it defensible. "escultura" is heard as art (the sculptília row), and his form is +2 syllables on a colon already long; option 3.
